topic: RBI decision day: your rights when a floating loan rate resets
caption:
RBI decides on rates today. If your home loan is on a floating rate, here are 4 things your lender must do when that rate resets.

Under RBI's rules for EMI-based floating-rate loans, the lender must tell you right away what the reset does to your EMI and tenure. You get to choose: a higher EMI, a longer tenure, or a mix. You can prepay, in part or in full, at any time. And the lender must offer the option to switch to a fixed rate, under its board-approved policy (*how many switches and what charges apply depend on that policy). You also get a statement every quarter showing principal and interest paid, EMIs left and the annual rate.

Why the choice matters, in an illustrative example: a ₹50 lakh, 20-year loan whose rate goes from 8% to 8.25%. Raising the EMI by about ₹781 adds roughly ₹1.9 lakh of interest over the loan. Keeping the EMI and extending the tenure by about 12 months adds roughly ₹5 lakh. This assumes the new rate holds for the full loan; your numbers will differ.

Save this for your next rate reset. Send it to someone with a home loan. Follow for one money fix a day.

Sources: RBI circular on reset of floating interest rate on EMI-based personal loans (18 Aug 2023, updated 1 Oct 2025); RBI policy preview as reported (2 Oct 2026). Interest figures are illustrative, calculated by us.
